definitions.explanation: The New Year celebration period in Japan, typically the first few days of January.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}は{家族|かぞく}で{過|す}ごす。
examples.english: I spend New Year's with my family.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}に{実家|じっか}に{帰|かえ}る。
examples.english: I go back to my parents' home for New Year's.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}におせち{料理|りょうり}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat osechi ryori during New Year's.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}には{初詣|はつもうで}に{行|い}く{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people go for their first shrine visit during New Year's.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころ、お{正月|しょうがつ}にお{年玉|としだま}をもらうのが{楽|たの}しみだった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I looked forward to receiving New Year's money.

notes:
お{正月|しょうがつ} is the most important holiday period in Japan, traditionally celebrated for the first three days of January ({三|さん}が{日|にち}). The お- prefix is honorific; {正月|しょうがつ} is the plain form.

CULTURAL TRADITIONS:
- {初詣|はつもうで}: first shrine visit of the year
- おせち{料理|りょうり}: traditional New Year foods
- お{年玉|としだま}: money given to children
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}: New Year greeting cards
- {門松|かどまつ}: pine decorations placed at entrances

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{正月|しょうがつ}を{迎|むか}える: to welcome the New Year
- お{正月|しょうがつ}{気分|きぶん}: New Year's mood
- お{正月|しょうがつ}{休|やす}み: New Year's holiday

USAGE:
Many businesses close from December 29 to January 3. Families typically gather at the {実家|じっか} (parents' home) during this period.
